messages:
alex: Heads-up — saw several pending GPU pods in eu-west last night, CA didn't scale a new p4 node for ~9m :thinking:
maya: ugh, logs?
alex: https://logs.internal/replay/xyz — back-to-back pending due to binpack on CPU pools, but we have a smaller GPU pool with Spot taints.
carlos: hmm are those pods marked safe-to-evict? CA won't evict GPU pods unless annotated.
maya: we annotate most with cluster-autoscaler.kubernetes.io/safe-to-evict=true, but this class is stateful and we left it out.
dena: I think the bigger issue is expander + scale-up granularity. Current CA is --expander=most-pods so it prefers a nodegroup that fits more pods instead of spinning up a matching GPU node.
alex: yeah — proposed change: switch to --expander=least-waste + --balance-similar-node-groups, and lower --scale-up-delay after-failure to 30s for faster retries.
maya: can we add a constraint so CA prefers on-demand GPU nodepools over spot for critical workloads? We had many preemptions.
carlos: we can surface a custom node group priority via node-group labels + the priority expander (we're on a fork that supports --expander=priority). If not, use price&least-waste heuristics and set spot nodegroups with taint: node.kubernetes.io/spot=true and tolerate only for noncritical pods.
dena: also tune --max-node-provision-time=15m -> keep it, but adjust --max-total-unready-percentage=40 to be more lenient during region capacity pressure.
alex: quick CA arg snippet I'm testing:
```
--expander=least-waste
--balance-similar-node-groups=true
--scale-down-unneeded-time=15m
--scale-down-utilization-threshold=0.5
--scan-interval=20s
--max-node-provision-time=15m
--skip-nodes-with-local-storage=false
```
maya: two comments: 1) skip-nodes-with-local-storage=false can be risky with ephemeral stateful pods; ensure PodDisruptionBudgets are in place. 2) lowering scale-down-unneeded-time to 15m might increase churn — probably fine for gpu pools but watch billing.
carlos: we should also set nodeTemplate labels to indicate capacity type and a custom annotation used by a CA webhook: redwood.ai/node-priority=high|spot so we can implement a small admission controller to prefer high for certain workloads.
dena: for spot handling, explicit patching approach: spot nodepools have taint spot=true:NoSchedule and we only allow pods with tolerations and a label workload=best-effort. That prevents CA from choosing spot for stateful GPUs.
alex: I pushed a test DaemonSet to annotate new GPU job pods with safe-to-evict when they are checkpointed; reduces eviction risk.
sre-bot: incident created: #INC-2026 — high pending GPU pods (eu-west) — assigned to @carlos, @maya
maya: next steps I propose:
- roll CA flags to staging with snippet above
- create admission webhook for node-priority labels (low risk)
- adjust nodegroup taints and tolerations for spot vs on-demand
- add Prom rule for pending_gpu_pod_time > 5m alert
any objections?
carlos: +1, will own the webhook and staging rollout. I'll leave a runbook for rollback: revert --expander and scale-up delay.
dena: I'll open a short eval to quantify cost delta if we prefer on-demand for 20% of GPU capacity vs mix.
alex: thanks — will coordinate the staging deploy and runbook. ping if anything blocks. :thumbsup:
